primitives.name: Receptor-Effector Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: The function of one group of receptors (the drive receptors) is to transmit to the motor apparatus, via the brain, activating impulses corresponding to the nature and intensity of the need as it arises.
primitives.assumptions: Receptors map need intensity to motor output linearly with time delay.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When N(t) exceeds threshold, R(t) saturates and M(t) becomes non-linear.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian update P(M|N) mirrors receptor-effector transmission; GSE state transition P(M'|M) reflects motor adaptation.
layer2.telemetry: Neural spike rate vs. behavioral latency

primitives.name: Behavioral Trial-and-Error
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this way innate behavior tendencies are organized on a genuine but primitive trial-and-error basis.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B_i(t)': 'behavioral act i at time t (dimensionless)', 'E_i': 'efficacy of act i (dimensionless)', 'T': 'trial duration (seconds)'}
primitives.assumptions: Behavioral efficacy E_i follows a probabilistic reward model with diminishing returns.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E_i < 0.1, behavior is reinitialized via random walk.

primitives.name: Need Intensity Gradient
primitives.verbatim_quote: Probably through the action of these drive receptors and receptor-effector connections preëstablished by the processes of organic evolution, the various needs evoke actions which increase in intensity and variety as the need becomes more acute.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'dN/dt': 'rate of need change (dimensionless/second)', 'I(t)': 'intensity of need (dimensionless)', 'A(t)': 'action intensity (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Action intensity A(t) is proportional to dN/dt with a lag factor.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When dN/dt > 1, A(t) enters chaotic regime due to sensory overload.

layer2.mapping: GSI models I(t) as a latent variable in a Gaussian process; GSE maps A(t) to state-space control inputs.
layer2.telemetry: Sensory input rate vs. motor output variance

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism of innate behavior is modeled as a feedback loop between need states and motor responses. Drive receptors encode need intensity N(t), which activates motor impulses M(t) through a receptor-effector pathway. As N(t) increases, the system evolves toward higher action intensity A(t), reflecting biological urgency. This dynamic is governed by a trial-and-error process where behavioral efficacy E_i is evaluated empirically. When environmental conditions vary, rigid mappings fail, necessitating flexible behavioral repertoires. The system thus operates under a stochastic policy where actions are selected based on prior success rates. In GSI, this translates into Bayesian inference over behavioral outcomes; in GSE, it becomes a Markov decision process optimizing for need resolution. The gradient of need intensity provides temporal modulation, while the trial-and-error framework enables adaptive learning. The system's robustness stems from redundancy—multiple action sequences can resolve a need, ensuring survival even under environmental uncertainty.
